newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money falls to five percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money falls to five percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money fell to five percent from eight percent on Wednesday morning on the back of ample liquidity, dealers said.
They said the usual government transfer of civil servants salaries at month-end, together with central bank supply of 226 billion rupiah, kept the market ample.
One state bank dealer said many operators were also seen unloading rupiah they had held earlier on speculation of a possible interest rate by the U.S. Federal Reserve.
But the Federal Reserve kept its rates unchanged.
Longer-term rates, and swap rates, softened following ample supply at the short-end. One- and three-month money were at 13.00/13.25 percent and 13.75/14.25 percent, respectively.

Dealers said the market was quiet due to a public holiday in Singapore. The Jakarta market will be closed on Thursday for a public holiday. There will also be no clearing with the central bank on May 29 due to the general election.
The central bank offered 5-6 day bilateral papers (SBIs) at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent and three-month at 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 7.61 percent, compared with 9.92 percent on Monday.
Bond dealers said the market was quiet, with prices remaining stable.
